title: Microsoft Purview retention: what is kept, what is deleted and who decides
summary: The policy-status PowerShell command omits a switch Microsoft requires for accurate distribution information. The page also overlooks Graph-based policy monitoring and omits the version from its Graph label-creation endpoint; most of the retention, licensing and portal guidance is supported.

claims.claim: Purview retention determines how long Microsoft 365 content, including Copilot interactions, is retained and deleted.
claims.quote: Use a retention policy to manage the data for your organization by deciding proactively whether to retain content, delete content, or retain and then delete the content.

claims.claim: Retention policies assign the same retention settings at the mailbox, site or other container level.
claims.quote: A retention policy lets you do this very efficiently by assigning the same retention settings at the container level to be automatically inherited by content in that container.

claims.claim: Retention labels assign retention settings at item level, including folders, documents and emails.
claims.quote: Use a retention policy to assign the same retention settings for content at a site or mailbox level, and use a retention label to assign retention settings at an item level (folder, document, email).

claims.claim: Retention settings use retain and delete actions.
claims.quote: Use a retention policy to manage the data for your organization by deciding proactively whether to retain content, delete content, or retain and then delete the content.

claims.claim: Retention can retain only, delete only, or retain and then delete.
claims.quote: | Retention settings that can retain and then delete, retain-only, or delete-only | Yes | Yes |

claims.where: What it is: content stays in place
claims.claim: Content with retention settings remains in its original location.
claims.quote: When content has retention settings assigned to it, that content remains in its original location.

claims.claim: Editing or deleting retained content causes a copy to be retained.
claims.quote: But if they edit or delete content that's included in the retention policy, a copy of the content is automatically retained.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive retain the copy in the Preservation Hold library.
claims.quote: For SharePoint and OneDrive sites: The copy is retained in the Preservation Hold library.

claims.claim: Exchange mailboxes retain the copy in Recoverable Items.
claims.quote: For Exchange mailboxes: The copy is retained in the Recoverable Items folder.

claims.claim: Retained copies for Teams, Viva Engage messages, Copilot and AI apps use the hidden SubstrateHolds folder.
claims.quote: For Teams, Viva Engage messages, Copilot and AI apps: The copy is retained in a hidden folder named SubstrateHolds as a subfolder in the Exchange Recoverable Items folder.

claims.claim: Retention-policy settings do not follow content moved outside its container.
claims.quote: However, the retention settings don't travel with the content in its new location. If that's required, use retention labels instead of retention policies.

claims.claim: Retention-label settings follow content moved within the Microsoft 365 tenant.
claims.quote: Unlike retention policies, retention settings from retention labels travel with the content if it's moved to a different location within your Microsoft 365 tenant.

claims.claim: Retention-policy settings are not applied manually.
claims.quote: | Retention settings applied manually | No | Yes |

claims.claim: Retention labels can be applied manually.
claims.quote: Enable people in your organization to apply a retention label manually to content in Outlook and Outlook on the web, OneDrive, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365 groups.

claims.claim: Adaptive scope membership is evaluated daily using a query against selected attributes.
claims.quote: An adaptive scope uses a query that you specify, so the membership isn't static but dynamic by running daily against the attributes or properties that you specify for the selected locations.

claims.claim: A static scope covers all instances of a location or specific inclusions and exclusions.
claims.quote: A static scope doesn't use queries and is limited in configuration in that it can apply to all instances for a specified location, or use inclusion and exclusions for specific instances for that location.

claims.claim: Retention takes precedence over deletion, subject to the priority-cleanup exception described later.
claims.quote: By default, retention always takes precedence over permanent deletion, and the longest retention period wins.

claims.claim: The longest retention period for the item wins when multiple settings retain it.
claims.quote: If content is subject to multiple retention settings that retain content for different periods of time, the content is retained until the end of the longest retention period for the item.

claims.claim: A retention label's delete action takes precedence over a retention policy's delete action.
claims.quote: This means that a delete action from a retention label always takes precedence over a delete action from any retention policy.

claims.claim: For deletion conflicts among policies, adaptive or specifically included scopes take precedence over org-wide scopes.
claims.quote: If a retention policy for a location uses an adaptive scope or a static scope that includes specific instances (such as specific users for Exchange email) that retention policy takes precedence over a static scope that is configured for all instances for the same location.

claims.claim: The shortest deletion period resolves remaining policy deletion conflicts.
claims.quote: The shortest deletion period wins. Applicable to determine when items will be deleted from retention policies and the outcome couldn't be resolved from the previous level: Content is permanently deleted at the end of the shortest retention period for the item.

claims.claim: Preservation Lock has no UI control and must be applied with PowerShell.
claims.quote: You must use PowerShell if you need to use Preservation Lock. Because administrators can't disable or delete a policy for retention after this lock is applied, enabling this feature is not available in the UI to safeguard against accidental configuration.
claims.fix: Keep the PowerShell guidance, but qualify the note: 'The Preservation Lock guide says enabling the lock is not available in the UI. The Get-RegulatoryComplianceUI reference separately describes a preservation-lock checkbox; Microsoft documentation is inconsistent.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-regulatorycomplianceui?view=exchange-ps alongside the existing guide.
